messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> SEV2: streaming.gateway.p99 > 10s (eu-west-1). Triggered 2026-03-15T02:03:54Z. Affected: /v1/stream/* (SSE + WS). Alerts: high socket stall, backpressure spike, proxy write_timeouts. Runbook: https://dash.internal/redwood/runbooks/streaming-backpressure

Maria Lopez: ack, I'm oncall. Pulling dashboards now -> https://dashboards.internal/redwood/d/streaming-tail. Will triage p95/p99 and check recent deploys.

Dan Kim: handed over — I was debugging earlier. Noticed proxy config change rolled at 02:10 UTC (ingress/proxy keepalive/frame-size tweaks). After that we saw a step increase in client retransmits and socket stalls. I tried a soft restart of one proxy node, p99 dipped then climbed back. Leaving notes below.

Alice Chen: adding logs snippet from proxy around 02:12 UTC:
```
[streaming-proxy-2] 2026-03-15T02:12:21Z WARN upstream write timeout after 5s for conn 10.1.2.9 route=/v1/stream/session
[streaming-proxy-2] 2026-03-15T02:12:21Z DEBUG chunk-flush-latency=8200ms backlog=120
[streaming-proxy-2] 2026-03-15T02:13:03Z INFO client-window=512 drop-bytes=0
```

eng-rt: telemetry shows p95 ~ 1.2s but p99 jumped from 3s -> 12s in last 10m. Error fraction (stream stalls >5s) ~ 4.8% globally, eu-west-1 ~ 9.6%. Top customer impact: 24k streams in window, ~2.3k stalled >5s.

CS Liaison: cascade - we have two customers opening tickets: AcmeCorp (prod) and LobsterCo (staging). Both report long delays in live updates, one reported UI hang and manual reconnect. No major data loss reported yet.

Nora Patel: SLO check: streaming p99 target 5s. Current p99 12s -> SLO breach. Notifying trusts/enterprise channels after mitigation.

Maria Lopez: quick plan: 1) rollback proxy keepalive/frame tweak if safe, 2) scale streaming-proxy replicas + restart (gradual), 3) temporarily enable http-streaming-fallback to chunked-polling for affected customers, 4) increase proxy write_timeout to 15s as a stopgap, 5) collect tcp dumps for problematic clients. I'll run 1-3 now.

Dan Kim: FYI the config tweak was this PR: https://git.internal/redwood/proxy/merge/2048 — it reduced default write_timeout and introduced a small output coalescer. We suspected it would help tails but might interact poorly with client backpressure. Rollback safe? It touches live traffic but non-invasive to model plane.

Maria Lopez: performing rollback step 1 -> issuing kubectl rollout undo
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/streaming-proxy --to-revision=2047
kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/streaming-proxy
```

sre-rotation: I'm increasing replicas from 4 -> 8 in eu-west-1 to reduce per-proxy load and give room for restarts. Command issued.

Alice Chen: while rollback starts, run a synthetic SSE client to validate chunking behavior:
```
# sanity check
curl -N -v "https://eu.gateway.redwood/v1/stream/test?mode=synthetic" | sed -n '1,40p'
# expect periodic events, no 5s+ stalls
```

Maria Lopez: also enabling temp feature-flag "http_stream_fallback: true" for top-ten customers via /flags API for quick mitigation (falls back to chunked polling).

eng-rt: telemetry note: after first restart of a proxy instance p99 dropped from 12s -> 6.5s for 40s, then trended back up. Looks correlated with connection backlog on particular upstream host pool.

Dan Kim: I'm seeing elevated RTOs on the upstream edge (ALB) in the same timeframe. Might be client-side slow consumers triggering backpressure that accumulates in the proxy buffers. Could be exacerbated by the output coalescer.

Maria Lopez: mitigation update 02:22 UTC — rollback completed to revision 2047, replicas scaled to 8, feature-flag enabled for top-10. Monitoring -> initial telemetry shows p99 improved to ~5.8s. Keeping watch for 15m.

CS Liaison: informed AcmeCorp via support -> they're trying the fallback and report much better responsiveness for now. :thumbsup:

Alice Chen: collected tcpdump sample on one node (s3 link): s3://telemetry/streams/8460001234/tcpdump-node2.pcap. Will attach to postmortem.

eng-rt: reducing chunk flush interval on runtime to avoid big flushes; pushing runtime override to EU cluster (hotpatch):
```
POST /admin/runtime/override
{ "streaming.flush_interval_ms": 50 }
```

Dan Kim: quick check: any recent client-side SDK change? CS says no. Also pushing a small ALB idle timeout bump in eu-west-1 from 60s -> 120s to tolerate slow reads (open to objections).

Maria Lopez: ALB change queued, will coordinate with infra. For now main mitigations: rollback + scale + fallback + runtime override. Observability: enabling extended logs for 30m on streaming-proxy.

Nora Patel: marking incident state -> active. Impact: partial customer degradation, SLO breached. Notifying legal/compliance? Not yet.

sre-rotation: monitoring window 02:30-02:45 UTC. If p99 stays <6s we'll move to recovery. If it spikes again we escalate to Sev1.

Maria Lopez: update 02:33 UTC: p99 4.9s, p95 1.1s, stalled fraction down to 1.1% in eu-west-1. Good trend. Leaving tracing on for next 30m.

Dan Kim: leaving handoff notes to Maria in the incident board -> will join if needed. Also adding remediation: revert output coalescer change in next patch release and add perf-testing harness for slow clients.

CS Liaison: customers notified, support triage updated.

Maria Lopez: will keep this thread updated. Next update at 02:45 UTC or earlier if there is regression. If stable for 30m we'll move to mitigated and start timeline/postmortem. :white_check_mark:
